title: AI Study Assistants for IB: Exam Prep and Coursework
summary: Discover how AI study assistants help IB students prepare for exams and improve IA, EE, and TOK coursework with criteria-aligned feedback.
body_markdown:
## AI-Powered Tools for IB Exam Preparation and Coursework


AI-powered study assistants can help IB students connect daily revision with coursework improvement. The useful distinction is between a general chatbot that produces broad explanations and an IB-focused platform that organizes syllabus content, exam-style practice, progress data, and coursework feedback around the way IB work is assessed.


RevisionDojo brings these functions into one platform. Its exam-preparation tools include IB Study Notes, Flashcards, Questionbank practice, Jojo AI, mock exams, predicted papers, and progress tracking. Its Coursework Grader supports subject Internal Assessments, Extended Essays, and Theory of Knowledge essays, giving students criterion-level feedback based on the selected IB subject and assessment type.


This does not make AI a replacement for your teacher, supervisor, or your own academic judgment. It gives you a structured way to identify gaps, test your understanding, and revise drafts before asking a teacher to review the next version.


### Comprehensive IB Exam Preparation


An effective IB study assistant should reduce the time spent searching for disconnected resources. Instead of moving between a generic chatbot, random online notes, and separate practice websites, students can follow a connected workflow: learn a topic, retrieve it from memory, answer an exam-style question, review the feedback, and repeat the weak areas.


### How AI supports IB revision


RevisionDojo is designed as an all-in-one IB study platform. Students can select their programme and subjects, then move between resources that serve different stages of preparation:


- **Study Notes** explain syllabus topics in a structured format.
- **Flashcards** support active recall and spaced repetition.
- **Questionbank** practice lets students work through questions by subject, topic, level, paper, or question type.
- **Jojo AI** explains difficult concepts, answers follow-up questions, and creates targeted practice.
- **Mock Exams and Exam Mode** provide timed practice under exam-like conditions.
- **Analytics and progress tracking** show which topics have been attempted, completed, or marked for review.
- **Predicted Papers and exam-building tools** help students assemble broader practice sessions as examinations approach.


These tools are useful because IB performance depends on more than recognizing a definition. Students need to apply concepts to unfamiliar material, respond to command terms, show working where required, interpret sources or data, and manage time across a paper. A study assistant organized by IB subject and syllabus topic can make those demands visible during revision rather than during the final examination.


### A practical study loop


A productive session can be short and specific. Choose one topic, read the relevant Study Notes, ask Jojo AI about a point you cannot explain, create or review a small Flashcard set, and then complete targeted Questionbank items without looking at the answer first.


After marking the questions, record the exact reason for each error. The problem might be missing knowledge, a misread command term, weak evidence, incorrect calculation, or an answer that is too descriptive. Return to the topic only when the error analysis tells you what needs attention.


For example, a Biology student who repeatedly loses marks when explaining a process should not simply reread the whole chapter. They can ask Jojo AI to distinguish description from explanation, practise questions using the relevant command terms, and compare later answers with the feedback. A Mathematics student can use topic filters to separate algebraic errors from errors caused by interpreting a graph or selecting an unsuitable method.


### Analytics should support decisions, not replace them


AI-driven analytics are valuable when they lead to a clear action. A dashboard showing that you have completed many questions is less useful than a record showing that you consistently miss evaluation questions in a particular unit or lose marks in one section of a paper.


Use progress data to decide:


1. Which topics require immediate review.
2. Which mistakes recur across several questions.
3. Whether your accuracy changes under timed conditions.
4. Whether improvement transfers from topic practice to complete papers.
5. Which subject deserves attention when several deadlines compete.


RevisionDojo’s connected workflow is designed to move from knowledge to application and then to correction. Jojo AI can explain an idea, but the Questionbank and timed practice reveal whether you can use that idea without assistance. That distinction matters when preparing for an externally assessed IB examination.


### AI Coursework Grading and Feedback


IB coursework requires a different kind of support from exam revision. An exam question usually has a mark scheme for a particular response, whereas an IA, EE, or TOK essay is developed over multiple drafts and judged against criteria concerning investigation, argument, analysis, reflection, communication, or justification.


The International Baccalaureate uses both internal and external assessment in the Diploma Programme. Internal Assessment work is generally completed during the course and marked by teachers before moderation or external assessment arrangements, while components such as the Extended Essay and TOK essay are assessed through the IB system. Feedback should therefore be connected to the relevant rubric, not based only on general writing advice.


### What the RevisionDojo Coursework Grader supports


RevisionDojo’s Coursework Grader supports the following categories:


Coursework type Support described by the platform


Subject Internal Assessment IB subject IAs across supported subjects, with SL or HL selection where applicable


Subject Extended Essay IB subject EEs with the relevant subject and level or rubric selection


Theory of Knowledge essay TOK essay feedback using the relevant TOK assessment criteria


The grader does not describe itself as a general-purpose marker for every IB task. The supported list is **subject IAs, subject EEs, and TOK essays** . Students should select the exact subject, level, coursework category, and rubric before submitting a draft so that feedback is interpreted against the correct assessment framework.


### How criteria-based AI feedback works


A typical workflow begins with uploading a draft, choosing the coursework type and subject details, and requesting a report. The resulting feedback includes annotations, a performance breakdown by criterion, and prioritized suggestions for the next draft. Students can then revise a specific weakness rather than making broad changes without knowing what problem they are solving.


For an IA, feedback might identify a research question that is too broad, evidence that does not support the conclusion, a method that is insufficiently justified, or analysis that remains descriptive. For an EE, the focus may be the relationship between the research question, argument, sources, analysis, and reflection. For a TOK essay, the student may need to improve connections between claims, counterclaims, real-life examples, areas of knowledge, and the prescribed title.


RevisionDojo positions its Coursework Grader as built specifically for IB coursework using insights from real IB examiners. The platform is not an official IB examiner and its report is not an official grade. Its role is to provide a draft-stage review that helps students understand how their work may be read against the selected criteria before discussing revisions with a teacher or supervisor.


### Use AI feedback without compromising academic integrity


AI feedback should help you evaluate and improve your own work, not write a submission for you. The IB states that it will not ban AI software, but work produced by an AI tool is not regarded as the student’s own. If AI-generated text, images, or graphs are used in assessed work, the use must be made clear and referenced according to the school’s requirements and the IB’s academic-integrity guidance.


A safe coursework workflow is therefore:


- Write your research question, argument, analysis, and reflection yourself.
- Use the grader to identify weaknesses and explain relevant criteria.
- Check every suggestion against your subject guide and teacher feedback.
- Rewrite in your own words and preserve your own reasoning.
- Keep records of drafts, feedback, sources, and major decisions.
- Ask your teacher or supervisor how AI use should be acknowledged.


Do not treat a predicted mark as a final result. AI can misunderstand a subject-specific requirement, overlook context, or give advice that is too general. The strongest use of a Coursework Grader is iterative: submit a genuine draft, study the criterion-level comments, make defensible changes, and confirm the direction with the person supervising your work.


### Why integration matters for IB students


Exam preparation and coursework are often managed as separate projects, even though both require the same underlying habits: understanding criteria, applying subject knowledge, responding to feedback, and tracking improvement. An all-in-one platform reduces the need to rebuild your workflow for every subject and assessment type.


A student might use Study Notes and Questionbank practice to prepare for Biology exams, Jojo AI to clarify a difficult concept, and the Coursework Grader to review a Biology IA draft. The tools address different tasks, but the student can manage them through one study system and use progress information to decide what to do next.


The important test is not whether an AI platform produces a large amount of material. It is whether the platform helps you move from explanation to independent practice, from draft to specific revision, and from feedback to measurable improvement. RevisionDojo’s combination of IB exam preparation and examiner-informed coursework grading is designed around that sequence.
